transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… it’s mostly work. I mean, it’s not one little thing, it’s like I keep forgetting stuff I really should not be forgetting. Scheduled callbacks, work orders, follow-ups I told people I’d do — like I’ll say, “Yes, I’ll call you back,” or “I’ll check on that and get it moving,” and then somehow it just slips, and by the time I realize it, there’s already another thing stacked on top of it.

And it’s gotten to where it’s not just embarrassing anymore, it’s causing problems. People are waiting on me, coworkers have to ask me if I did things, and I hate that because I’m not trying to be careless. I work maintenance and repair, so there’s always something that needs tracking, and I feel like I’m constantly losing pieces of the day. Now it’s piled up bad enough that work basically told me I need to come in and get this looked at before I mess up my chance at moving up. That’s really what brought me here.
Have you noticed yourself forgetting things or having trouble keeping track of tasks in other parts of your life, like at home or with friends, or is this mostly happening at work?

It’s mostly work where it’s become impossible to ignore. I mean, I’m sure at home I forget little things here and there, but what actually brought me in is the work stuff — scheduled callbacks, work orders, those basic follow-ups where I’ve told someone, “Yeah, I’ll take care of that,” and then I don’t circle back like I said I would.

And the thing is, it’s not like I don’t care. I’ll mean to do it, and then the day gets moving, another repair comes in, somebody asks me something, and then whatever I was supposed to track just kind of disappears from my head until later. By then it’s already caused a problem, or someone else has had to remind me, which feels awful.

It’s piled up enough now that work basically said I need to get it checked out, because if I keep going like this I could mess up my chance at moving up. So, yeah — mostly work, but it’s serious enough there that I can’t just brush it off anymore.
Have you found it hard to stay focused or pay attention, especially during tasks or conversations at work?

Yes, definitely. That’s actually one of the big things I notice at work. Like, I’ll open up a digital work order thinking, okay, I’ve got this, I just need to read the notes and figure out what the issue is. And then halfway through reading it, my mind just… I don’t know, it slips off. There’ll be a noise, or someone moving around, or I’ll suddenly think about the next job I’m supposed to get to, and then I look back at the screen and realize I have no idea what I just read.

And it’s not like the words are hard or anything. I can read it, but it doesn’t always stay with me. I’ll be staring right at the work order, but it’s like my attention already left the room. Then I have to start over, sometimes more than once, and that slows everything down. It’s frustrating because I feel like I should be able to just read the notes, understand them, and go do the repair, but I lose the thread really easily.

Looking back at when you were a child, did you have similar issues with forgetting things, losing track of tasks, or having trouble staying focused, or is this something that mostly started later in life?

Yeah… I mean, thinking back, I don’t think this is brand-new. Work is where it’s really catching up with me now, but I can remember being like this back in grade school, long before job pressure or anything like that.

Teachers would say I was bright, like I understood things, but I was always misplacing papers or not turning something in because I couldn’t find it, or I’d miss part of the directions even though I was sitting right there. I remember needing reminders to finish classwork, too — like I’d start it, and then somehow I’d lose track of what I was supposed to be doing, and the teacher would have to come back around and say, “Are you finished?” or “Keep going.”

So, yeah, it feels like the same kind of thing, just back then it was school papers and directions, and now it’s work orders and callbacks.
